claims: The nine frozen file hashes and manifest-order composite were independently recomputed and match the manifest.
The base longitudinal correction path is claim-addressed, and buildG21CurrentClaimView preserves source records as current or superseded claim projections with evidenceId, sourceLocator and audience.
The lifecycle path is not claim-safe: makeProfile gives a conflict one default claim equal to its whole content and unconditionally makes the correction supersede that claim.

For RANGE-INTERNAL-FORGE-I2, the conflict claim is the still-valid 64 percent confidence result, while the correction says to keep that result and only reject an unwillingness inference; the corrected current view nevertheless retires the conflict claim.
For RANGE-INTERNAL-STORY-I3, the correction says to keep the association and remove causal use, but the same forced supersession retires the only claim containing the association.
The validator requires this whole conflict-claim retirement and the current-view tests compare emitted output to the same builder, so this broken lineage passes validation.

veto.failure: The lifecycle builder and validator retire still-valid claims. RANGE-INTERNAL-FORGE-I2 supersedes the only claim carrying the 64 percent confidence result even though its correction says to keep that result, and RANGE-INTERNAL-STORY-I3 similarly supersedes the association its correction says to preserve. Because these corrected projections pass validation, broken claim lineage can pass.
veto.resolvingTest: Split the affected lifecycle conflict records into claim-addressable assertions and change lifecycle validation so each direct correction supersedes only the false assertion. Add deterministic corrected-input tests proving that RANGE-INTERNAL-FORGE-I2 keeps the 64 percent confidence claim and RANGE-INTERNAL-STORY-I3 keeps the association claim current with their original evidenceId, sourceLocator and audience, while only the invalid inference or causal interpretation is superseded.
